coverage_note: Living registry, not a claim that every programming language has been exhausted. Direct AI-oriented rivals and adversarial compact-language families are tracked separately.

competitors.name: Sigil
competitors.kern_lane: cl100k_base and o200k_base on HumanEval+, MBPP+, and BigCodeBench
competitors.next_gate: Repeat when a newer public distribution changes converter or compiler behavior

competitors.name: Toke
competitors.kind: Compiled AI-native language with a native BPE tokenizer
competitors.public_claim: 52% average reduction across 42 programs with a purpose-built 16K BPE
competitors.kern_lane: 60 equivalent JSON-CLI pairs: Kern 3023 vs Toke 6347 cl100k tokens; Kern 60/60 vs Toke 29/60 public smoke probes
competitors.native_observation: Equal 16K vocabulary held-out contest: Kern native BPE 2870 tokens vs Toke native BPE 3906; Kern is 26.52% smaller and exact-round-trips 60/60
competitors.next_gate: Monitor Toke compiler, tokenizer, corpus, and public benchmark releases for material changes

competitors.name: KARN
competitors.kern_lane: 46 matched executable programs: Kern 670 vs KARN 685 cl100k tokens; both interpreters 46/46 exact stdout; KARN Python target 22/46
competitors.claim_audit: The advertised approximate 47-vs-198 REST row has no named tokenizer, paired sources, or counting script; current public KARN snippets use 72 and 118 cl100k tokens
competitors.native_observation: Kern native 16K uses 533 tokens versus KARN with its deployable cl100k lane at 685, 22.19% lower; shared-tokenizer result remains the neutral language comparison
competitors.next_gate: Monitor for publication of the exact claimed corpus, tokenizer, or a materially changed compiler

competitors.name: NERD
competitors.kind: LLVM-backed intermediate language for machine authorship
competitors.public_claim: 50-70% fewer tokens generally; its public table shows 32-33% below Python on FizzBuzz and four math functions
competitors.kern_lane: All 7 deterministic local examples: Kern 436 vs NERD 484 cl100k tokens; every Python, Kern, minifier, and NERD program matches its stdout oracle
competitors.claim_audit: NERD's public counter is the compiler lexer, not an LLM tokenizer. The current math definition reproduces 32 lexer tokens but FizzBuzz uses 43 rather than 49; paired Python sources and one common tokenizer are unpublished.
competitors.native_observation: Kern native 16K uses 367 tokens versus NERD + cl100k at 484, 24.17% lower; shared-tokenizer Kern is 9.92% lower
competitors.next_gate: Expand when NERD publishes a larger deterministic corpus, paired sources, native tokenizer, or generation benchmark

competitors.name: Ax
